Your Honour, so he was saying it in private and in public around October of 1991. Thank you. Now, interestingly enough, Your Honour, and clearly I'm going to have to put this exhibit up, later, a lot later, some -- in June of 1992, as recorded in, I think it's Glas almost certainly, although the publication isn't clear, Mr. Brdjanin used words that were not dissimilar. This is Exhibit P21. You can put that, please, on the ELMO, since we can't get anywhere on Sanction. I'm sorry, what did I say? I'm sorry, did I say 2-1? It's 2-5-1. Yes, I think if we can just put it down for a moment so we can see the top of it, please, usher, right down so we can see the top. No. Thank you. The headline is -- I still can't see it. It's dated the 16th of June 1992. Headline: "Indications of a war for the roads. The Autonomous Region of Krajina seeking a way out of the increasingly tighter grip of the traffic and economic blockade." And then if we could go back to the highlighted part, please, this is what Radoslav Brdjanin says: "If we do not manage to resolve the issue of annexing Krajina to Serbia peacefully, we shall literally have to resort to war," says Brdjanin. "In that case, the Muslim and Croat people will pay the price because they are precisely on the charted route of the future road." Your Honour, a lot later, and slightly odd in view of the already armed conflict that was going on, that those terms we would suggest are not dissimilar to those that were used by Karadzic. Your Honour, I say each time "we suggest" or "we submit" because you are the final deciders of fact, and we are merely put these proposals forward for your consideration. Yes, thank you. Can I have that back. Your Honour, this is all going to be rather boring, I'm afraid, because this is a section I'm going to show a lot of exhibits. I'm told it may be working again. Now, Your Honour, on the same day that Karadzic made his speech to the assembly that we just looked at, the 15th of October, the meeting of the SDS party council showed that the preparations were well advanced even at that early stage and that the means of putting into effect the creation of a Serbian state had been well thought out and that regionalisation was one of the top methods. Can I ask that Your Honours now have a look, and that I think, yes, it's up on the screen now, it's P20. We just look first of all at the minutes. It says, "Serbian Democratic Party, party council, 15th of October, minutes." It's on the screen. Then, Your Honours, if we go to the next page of that. And Your Honour, if we could highlight, if it's possible to highlight. We missed a page. Sorry. Yes, there it is. It's on the front page. I've a different version. Your Honour, if we highlight the words of Mr. Dutina, Your Honours I'm sure can see it. This is continuing along the same theme. "This evening, we must get rid of the illusion" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The print is too small. If we could enlarge it a little bit, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Blow it up. "This evening, we must shed the illusion that a form of coexistence with the Muslims and Croats can be found. Therefore, I suggest the following." And then he makes the following suggestions. Mr. Koljevic says, "Nothing can be done legally with the Party of Democratic Action, the SDA, and the Croatian Democratic Union." And if we go on to the next page, let's go on to the next page because I don't want to spend too long on this. If we go, please, to Mr. Neskovic's speech, and Your Honour, we suggest that this is absolutely the classic formulation of what the Serbs were doing at this time, which was provoking this crisis. "Since they will not revoke their decision" - and this, if you look above, is to do with the president of the constitutional court - "I suggest that a parliamentary crisis be provoked, demand new elections because in this way we would gain time which suits us. As regards outvoting, we were the first to use it at the local level and they at the republican level." And finally: "Go for a change of policy with the aim of creating a Greater Serbia." And Your Honour will know that this again, the term Greater Serbia is the subject of a lot of dispute, Your Honour. And then next, going to Mr. Djukic, Rajko Djukic, which I think we will see on the next page, to the top of that page, Djukic: "We should agree on who is to do what, because the whole job cannot be done by just a few people," and that is a matter of common sense. And as we say, this plan involved a large number of people at various levels. "We cannot leave the assembly or any other body. If the coalition does not withdraw its decision, activate parallel government bodies, primarily the Serbian Assembly." Your Honour, that is what happened as you've heard in the evidence in a number of municipalities where there was either a Muslim majority or equality, these Serbian assembly came into being. Your Honour, as I say, the variant A and B wasn't the beginning, by any stretch of the imagination, and was merely one of the steps in the course of the development of this plan. "Coordinate the work of the Serbian regions," and then, "Overwhelm the public with a wave of information." This point was made of the section in our final brief that dealt with media control. Your Honour, we're not saying this is unique to the Serbs. By no stretch of the imagination. We have no doubt at all that the same was happening in the Croatian parts and the Muslim parts and has always happened, but it's a fact that the control of the supply of information is a vital adjunct to any sort of control and putting into effect plans. And then Mr. Miskin, and Your Honour, as I say, this is why we say that the regions were so important, states first thing: "Continue regionalisation more intensively." And then, "A group of experts on constitutional law, inspire to defend legitimacy." And again, "Establish parallel bodies immediately so that we will be ready." For what? Five, and underlined by hand, "Organise militarily, especially in the towns, and give instructions to this effect in the municipal boards and local boards." And finally, back to the media: "We are not well organised in the media war." And Your Honour, I think that's all that I want to remind you of in that document. Thank you. Your Honour, as we say, the variant A and B document and the Djeric instructions of the 26th of April are merely putting flesh, we submit, on the bones, extending a little bit further. If one looks again at variant A and B, Your Honour, this is really dealing with some of the themes. I know Your Honours have looked at this a number of times. If one looks first of all at para 8 of the first stage which is on, I hope, the third page, just highlight paragraph 8, please. And I'm sorry, I'm reminded I haven't given the number of the exhibit. P97. "Information propaganda activities are to be intensified in order to inform the Serb people promptly and completely about the political and security situation in the municipality and further afield." If one looks at the second stage of variant A, paragraph 8 again, this is variant A, Your Honours, you will recall is the municipalities in which the Serbs are a majority. And here, paragraph 8: "In taking all these measures, attention should be paid to ensuring respect for the national and other rights of members of all nationalities and engage them later on in the government bodies which will be established by the Assembly of the Serb people in the municipality." Now, if we have a look, please, at the second stage for a variant B municipality, in other words, where the Serbs were not in a majority, Your Honour, there the paragraph -- there is no paragraph 8 for the -- the ones where they weren't in a majority, and that is, we say, a significant difference because in municipalities where the Muslims posed no threat, and the Croats, it was all right, and that was the intention then apparently, as I say, there was a clear change in the intention, that they should be absorbed into a government, but not in the municipalities where the Serbs were in a minority or not in the majority. Your Honours, finally, P157 on this aspect of matters, just to remind ourselves again of the instructions issued by Prime Minister Djeric on the 26th of April. And Your Honours, can I remind you of paragraphs 3 and 4. 3: "The crisis staff coordinates the functions of the authorities" - I emphasise - "coordinates the function of the authority in order to ensure the defence of the territories, the safety of the population and property, the establishment of government," and so on and so forth. 4: "The command of the TO and the police forces is under the exclusive authority of the professional staff. And therefore, any interference regarding the command of the TO and/or the use of the police forces must be prevented." Your Honours, as we say, as we can see from the later documents, these were -- this was a developing series of directions and orders because we say it's quite clear that if that was meant as a directive, it was not followed, and there were changes. And finally, Your Honour, on the next page, the much disputed final paragraph 14, well, not disputed, but subject to much comment by both sides: "The crisis staff shall convene and make decisions in the presence of all its members" - I emphasise - "take official minutes, issue written decisions, and submit weekly reports to the regional and state organisations of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." The Defence take the point that this document does not talk about a regional crisis staff, but the only regional authority in existence at the time of this document being issued, the 26th of April, was the Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly. And we have seen that the earlier documents, in October, all were talking about the importance of regionalisation. And we suggest even if it doesn't specifically talk about the -- a regional crisis staff, this is what it clearly meant. And as we shall see later, what everybody else seemed to have accepted, whether or not it was actually written down in that document. Now, Your Honour, the six strategic goals which had been set out by Karadzic on the 12th of May could realistically only be achieved by the forceful displacement of the Muslims and Croats from the territory that the Republika Srpska wished to claim as its own, for a variety of reasons; geographical, historical, the need to link up with Serbia proper. And that forceful displacement was not a by-product, we would submit, of a desire to remain in the famous wish to remain in Yugoslavia, which by early 1992 had been effectively reduced to Serbia and Montenegro, and of course, Kosovo. But we say it wasn't a by-product, but an integral part of the criminal plan and one which was given, we would submit, on the evidence, the highest priority. Interestingly enough, Your Honours, in one sense, that seems to be accepted by the Defence in the commentary that they made in their final brief, and this is at page 129, to the document produced on the 7th of June by the Sanski Unska group, that group of municipalities, because they said that, and this is bottom of page 128: "It is clear that these municipalities were upset by the belief that they were being neglected on economic matters. But more importantly, they believed that the ARK Crisis Staff was not acting on issues related to the movement of population and the purging of non-Serbs from the military. The leaders from these municipalities clearly believed that the strategic goals of the Serbian People were not being implemented by the ARK Crisis Staff." It goes on to say, and this the Prosecution dispute but I'll read this: "A plain reading of the 7th of June 1992 conclusions" - and they are in Exhibit P229 - "especially when considered against the backdrop of the strong individual leaders of these municipalities shows that these municipalities were rebelling against the ARK because Brdjanin was not acting upon important issues in line with the SDS policies and the six strategic objectives." Your Honour, the Prosecution say on the evidence Brdjanin was doing just that, but clearly from that document those leaders of those municipalities wanted things to go even further, quicker. But it seems to be accepted that the strategic objectives did require the displacement of the population in whatever form it took. Now, can I move to dealing with the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and with regionalisation and its part in that. The association of Bosnian Krajina municipalities, ZOBK, as it has become known because that's what the B/C/S or the proper name for it comes down to in an acronym. Your Honour, the goals of the Serbs needed a consolidation of Serb areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And so the concept of regionalisation which we have touched on briefly came about. And it was described by Mr. Sejmenovic, the Bosniak deputy from Prijedor, and he said: "Mr. Brdjanin, as one of the more prominent members of parliament, is a person I noticed only in the second half of 1991 when the debate took place on federal institutions, on the Yugoslav People's Army, and particularly the need to regionalise Bosnia. As far as I can remember, that's when Mr. Brdjanin spoke more often in the debate. As for the proposals to start reorganising the country, or rather re-establishing regions, he was one of the most prominent speakers. And as a matter of fact, he insisted the most that such proposals be put through parliament." Your Honour, I shall be dealing with Mr. Brdjanin's authority and the like tomorrow in one group. But Your Honour, we would say straight away that it is clear that even from 1991, Mr. Brdjanin was a person who had authority. Then he was asked, that is Mr. Sejmenovic, "Can you expand a little on what you mean by regionalisation?" "In that period of time, that is to say at the moment when the SDS MPs, primarily through Mr. Brdjanin, presented their demand that parliament approve the regionalisation of the country, in that stage, the SDS called that economic regionalisation. And they explained the need to do so due to economic necessity." And he then went on to describe the debates, and it was pointed out that there were already -- there was already regionalisation based on economic principles. And they -- then he goes on to say this: "It all boiled done to the following: That they wanted to create regions along the lines of the already established Serb regions in Croatia. And of course, it was noticed that they had started doing this in some parts of Bosnia even before this had been discussed in parliament." And then finally he was asked this, and I'll give the page reference to the whole quote that I've read in a moment: "From the point of view of your party or you in particular, what did the purpose of this regionalisation appear to be if not economic?" "The purpose was national, ethnic. And this was evident in the policy of the SDS of Croatia, in the area of the neighbouring country where there were Serb areas. They first called for economic regionalisation, and then they closed off that area and turned it into a Serb autonomous region. So we already had experience with the SDS policies in the wider area, and we also had experience in the area of Bosnia." And the whole quote is taken from transcript page 12097 to 8. Your Honour, this is, Your Honour, we say, not only important because it was clear to everyone what the purpose of this regionalisation was, but also to make the point that it cannot be said that the Bosnian Serbs could not foresee what was going to happen if they pursued these policies because everyone could see by the end of 1991 what had happened in Croatia and the violence that had taken place there. Now, Your Honour, it is asserted by the Defence effectively as a kind of mantra in the face of the overwhelming evidence to the contrary that this was intended to be a voluntary, multiethnic, economic association, and that is at page 23 of their final brief. Mr. Dodik, whose evidence is relied on for quite a lot by the Defence, again, one of the many witnesses that Your Honours will have to consider the credibility, the accuracy, the reliability of him, himself disapproved of that. And if Your Honours look, please, at the article which is 2354 -- I'm sorry, it's -- yes, in fact, Your Honour, can I first of all look at the statute, 2354. Your Honour, what's relied on by the Defence are Articles 1, which says that the various municipalities listed there have united together on the basis of voluntariness and for the purpose of effecting long-term cooperation, coordination of development plans, and realising of other common interests. And Article 11, which states that "each member municipality may leave the association of municipalities." And sets out the restrictions on that. And that's relied on for evidence of voluntariness. And Mr. Treanor agreed when he had Article 11 put to him that that did indeed sound as if it was a voluntary organisation. He actually agreed it at page 20907 to 8 and not, as put in the Defence trial brief, and this is the last time I'm going to make this rather pathetic point, T21907. Your Honour, it is possible for all people to make errors when dealing with so many documents. Your Honour, in addition to those articles, the Defence rely on the evidence of Messrs. Vidic and Mr. Dejanovic that -- both of whom were members of the association and its subsequent assembly. And Mr. Vidic -- Mr. Dejanovic came after Mr. Vidic, and both of them said almost identical things. "It's your opinion," it was put to Mr. Dejanovic, "that the ARK Assembly as you described it was an unserious organisation." He said: "Yes, all my opinion." "And not as a result of any discussion that you had with Mr. Vidic?" "No, not at all. It's my expression from that time. And not only mine." "And this description that you gave us of Hyde Park, everyone coming or going, and everyone voting, you never discussed that with Mr. Vidic?" And you may recall that, Your Honours. Now, Your Honour, they denied or Mr. Dejanovic denied he had any discussion before or after he gave evidence with Mr. Vidic about his description of the assembly. But Your Honours will have to assess the credibility of what they say in the light of some of the following evidence. First of all, Article 16, Your Honour, "The association of municipalities shall monitor the situation and coordinate activities for the organisation and implementation of preparations for All Peoples' Defence in accordance with the law, municipal defence plans, and the republican defence plan." Your Honour, it begs the question if this organisation was intended to be economic, then what on earth is it concerning itself with about defence? And now Mr. Dodik, who when this association was formed spoke to the press, and that is P2457. 18th of April 1991, founding session, I think was the 21st. "Hasty regionalisation." And then he explains, and I'm not going to go through it all, that in view of him and his party, the Alliance of Reform Forces, this -- the reformists have abstained from voting because they haven't received sufficient information. And if you look at the bottom of that page, Your Honour, "It is our opinion," he stated, "that essentially from the point of view of economy, there are elements that would justify thinking about regionalisation, but that the current political situation in Yugoslavia rules it out and forces its postponement. This means, we as parties were not engaged in all of this, I can personally consider it politically highly illiterate and impudent that certain municipal assemblies voted on the initiative, in spite of the fact that none of the deputies received any of the materials," and so on and so forth. And Mr. Dodik, in fact, also testified about that at page T -- transcript page 20458. Your Honour, then if we briefly look at two other exhibits, this is concerned with the voluntary nature of this association, P11 first of all. Item 3, Mr. Brdjanin where he states: "I propose that the statute be adopted today as it stands because we cannot have ZOBK on a voluntary basis. We cannot wait for public debate in the municipal assemblies and convene the community assembly every month." And that was the 14th of May, second session of the Assembly, 14th of May 1991. Your Honour, the agenda that was then pursued by this association was, we submit, clearly nothing to do with economics at all, but a political agenda. One looks at the 30th of May, P72, I hope to canter through this lot, it's a conclusion signed by -- on behalf, I think, actually of -- yes, it's "za," Mr. Kupresanin, "Bearing in mind the complexity of the political and constitutional crisis in Yugoslavia," and so on and so forth, conclusion: "The community of association of municipalities, Bosnian Krajina, will not accept any agreement on behalf -- on the part of the Bosnia and Herzegovina that Yugoslavia should be organised as a confederation," so on and so forth. And 3, because Mr. Brdjanin is a deputy, he is authorised to take those conclusions to the assembly. Your Honour, on the 6th of August 1991, there was the takeover of the Kozara transmitter. And Your Honours, on the 6th of August -- and I'm sorry, that isn't, I don't think, in -- no, it's not. Can I just ask that be put on the ELMO very briefly. There was an announcement by the assembly that there was an unofficial report that the BiH Ministry of the Interior was considering sending operative units to take control of the TV relay. And it says it's effectively, "We consider possible intervention by BH MUP forces to be useful at this moment in areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina where the Serbian people are threatened" - that's the last paragraph - "but that they weren't to intervene anywhere in that area." In fact, what happened, as Your Honours know - thank you, that's all; that was P14, I think, yes, P14 - was that - thank you - that was the day that the transmitter was taken over by a group consisting of the Wolves of Vucak led by Milankovic, in the main part, but also by other people. Your Honours have already seen the video, and I'm not going to play it again; it will take up too much time. The video is P1532, and there's a transcript which is .1. And part of that they lengthy video was an interview with Mladjenovic, the minister for information, then the editor of Glas, and then the removed editor of Glas, and then Mr. Grahovac, who in August of 1991 was in charge of the executive council, and they give an interview on the year's anniversary of the takeover. And the reporter there said to them: "The crucial role in this action was played by the now legendary Wolves from Vucak and their commander, Veljko Milankovic. Here are some of their memories." And then there's a gentleman called Kesic. And in his description of the takeover, he said this: "The preparations took two days. On Saturday, around 1600 hours, we had our cars, men, and uniforms ready. In civilian clothes, we moved to Gradip, where they waited for me, their commander. From there, we moved towards Europa. When we reached Europa, we were met by the politicians of the then-Autonomous Region of Krajina, that is Bosnian Krajina, who explained to us, in short, the political importance of the relay takeover." Now, Your Honour, this again deals were a number of different things. First, the fiction that ZOBK was anything other than a political organisation. Second, the importance of the control of the media, the technical means by which the media operated. And third, Your Honour, the close cooperation between the politicians and these gangs of so-called paramilitaries such as the Wolves of Vucak. These weren't out of control; these were executing the desires and the wishes of the leadership. Your Honour, the founding or the declaration of the ARK Assembly on the 16th of September 1991 was, we suggest, no more than the official announcement of a situation which had existed since the founding of ZOBK in April 1991. Your Honour, can I invite Your Honours to look at the description given by - I'm sorry, Your Honour - BT-95, can I invite Your Honours to look at the transcript 19500. Because Your Honour, he explained about the autonomous regions and how they did or did not work. Your Honour, finally on this, the so-called multiethnic nature of this assembly, Mr. Blagojevic, at the transcript 21820, identified six delegates who were not Serbs. He was looking at the list. I think it's P60. It said "The delegates to the assembly," and he was asked about that. He said, "I believe that this list, this is a list that belonged to the association of municipalities, those were the delegates that represented the association of municipalities." Put to him: "This says list of representatives in the Krajina?" And he said, "Yes." Question: "But you mean that the representatives never changed over the period?" And he said, "No." And that was at 21820. Your Honour, as to the political content of the ARK assemblies, that is really obvious, and I don't propose to take Your Honours through any of that save for one document. And it looks like I may have to do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just go back for a moment, please, to P1532. I read the part, Your Honours, to do with the man who was from the Wolves of Vucak, but I left out a part that Kupresanin spoke. It's the same video, 1532.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the part --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The transcript's not numbered, unfortunately. But Your Honour, we've got it up on the... It says clip 4. Your Honour, I should say I said erroneously that this was the first anniversary of the takeover. It looks as though it was, in fact, the third anniversary, because it's April 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In your brief, you do deal with that, and also make reference to Kupresanin's...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, Your Honour, can I just remind Your Honour of -- because basically, I'm now dealing with points that have been made by the Defence where Kupresanin said, "We knew even back then that a state cannot be a state without its radio, TV, and other media and without its currency. We, in the assembly of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, knew that nothing could be achieved with Muslims and Croats, the anti-Serbian coalition, and we were happy to part ways with them. We began the parting with the Autonomous Region of Krajina and continued with the takeover of the relay." And Your Honours, as I say, we make reference to it in our final brief. Your Honour, I also missed out two documents which I should have referred Your Honours to which deal with the clearly political, not to say military nature of the association of Bosnian Krajina municipalities. Your Honour, the first is the document which was marked as P15 dated the 24th of August. And I'm not going to go through it, but it was a document that was addressed to municipal staffs of volunteer units. "We hereby enclose the essay submitted at the session of the representatives of the municipalities of Bosnian Krajina on the occasion of the establishment of the command of Bosanska Krajina volunteer units." And in addition to that, Your Honour, on the 6th of September there was a communication from the assembly of ZOBK signed by Kupresanin. And I think this is actually signed by him as opposed to being on his behalf, and stamped, which deals with those volunteer forces. All of that before the assembly. Now, Your Honour, can I finally deal with the evidence given by Mr. Vidic and Dejanovic, that the assembly of the ARK wasn't a serious document -- serious document, organisation. Mr. Blagojevic had this to say. He was asked, again this is in cross-examination: "Did you tell the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor that the legal basis for the existence of the Autonomous Region of Krajina was amendment 42 to Article 276 of the Bosnia-Herzegovina constitution?" And he said: "Yes." "And that was your understanding as a lawyer?" And he said: "Yes." And this is at transcript 21804. And then a little later, it was put to him: "There is no question, is there, Mr. Blagojevic, that these regional governments were important functioning parts of the Serbian authorities?" And he said: "Yes. In view of their authorisations at all events, yes." "But as a matter of practical reality," question, "these governments, these regional governments, whatever happened later, were important for the functioning of the Serbian Republic." "Well probably, yes. Probably." That's at 21856. Your Honour, can I move now to the crisis staffs. The Defence, in their final brief at pages 30 to 31, state that the legality of the ARK Crisis Staff was questionable. And I'm summarising. The Prosecution does not dissent from this view in any way. The legality of the whole creation, the strict legality of the whole creation of the Republika Srpska, the parallel assemblies established in municipalities like Prijedor, Krupa, Sanski Most, and their resulting crisis staff all are open to question as a matter of strict legality. But this isn't a case, Your Honour, about strict legality. This is a case about whether these institutions, legal or not legal, by whatever standards were applied, exercised authority and whether individual members, in this case, Mr. Brdjanin, used that authority and the institution to promote the commission of criminal acts. In December of 1991, we had the variant A and B instructions. On the 26th of January -- 22nd of January 1992, there is an intercept which I would invite Your Honours just quickly to look at. It's P2367, and it's page 7 of that intercept. The front page shows us it's the 22nd of January, and it's a conversation between Cizmovic and Karadzic. And there, Cizmovic is telling Karadzic, "Tonight, we also establish the crisis staff which will act when nobody can get together, when they can assemble more quickly." And he says, "Excellent." "So that's working. Because the objective must be carried out, instructions must be carried out." Now, Your Honour, the Defence say in response to that intercept which they don't dispute, there is no evidence that it ever happened. Well, in the sense of somebody coming along producing a document showing "here are the members," no. Or somebody going to one of the meetings and saying, "I attended those meetings," there is no evidence. But if we look at the surrounding evidence, we can see that - and this is the period very closely after the December instructions - the municipalities who could be described as coming within the variant B area started to set up crisis staffs. I use the word "covertly," because they weren't publicly announced because, for example, in Sanski Most, P750, which is a sort of running description of what happened with the SDS during the period, states that the crisis staff was set up on the 15th of January of 1992. Its formal declaration, its formal appearance into the public eye came on the 21st of April 1992, and that can be seen from P619. In Prijedor, the crisis staff actually started to be formed on the 27th of December 1991. That can be seen in Exhibit P1156. But it was actually formally declared on the 20th of May 1992, P1268. Now, Your Honour, the Defence make the point that that shows that these municipalities were setting up crisis staffs independent of the regional. Well, Your Honour, that's absolutely right. They were being set up not as a result of instructions from the regional, but instructions from the main board of the SDS. But equally, so was the regional crisis staff coming into existence because if it wasn't in existence covertly, then when on the 24th of February 1992, look, please at P116, what was the executive board of the SDS, Mr. Djukic, again, doing appointing Mr. Vukic, the coordinator of the SAO Krajina, and then setting out his duties, one of which was to take part in the work of the SAO Krajina crisis staff. Your Honour, that is why we say even though the April instructions themselves specifically don't say "regional crisis staff," it is absolutely clear on the evidence that the SDS intended and did establish a regional crisis staff. Your Honour, on the 14th of March 1992, at the SDS conference, and if we can look, please, at -- press conference, I should say, P127, 14th of March, there was a conference of the SDS Krajina -- Bosnian Krajina party. There was an assembly. Talks about the army and so on and so forth. And then: "The SDS crisis staff will be reinforced with a military council." Your Honour, if it was nonexistent, this is the most extraordinary series of documents and statements. Now, Your Honour, on the 3rd of April 1992, there was the crisis staff that apparently came into existence because of the SOS. Your Honour, I've already dealt with the Defence assertion that really all they were were a disaffected group of soldiers. The circumstances surrounding this, the invasion of the SOS, Your Honours have heard a number of times, and I'm going to just recap the major aspects of it. Your Honours have seen the newspaper article which sets out in full, P137, which has just come up on the screen for you, "The word of the warrior." Your Honour, the only sensible inference to be drawn from all the evidence is that this group was used as part of the SDS strategy to create this climate of fear that would enable them to put their plan into effect. Now, criticism is made by the Defence of that suggestion, assertion, inference that we invite you to draw. Your Honour, can I just recap those circumstances. Into Banja Luka come this group of armed men who set up barricades. Banja Luka is the seat of then the 5th Krajina Corps, the biggest corps in the JNA. It is seat of the CSB, not to mention the various SJBs of the police. Nobody attempts to take down those barricades or do anything. They present a list of demands which bear a remarkable similarity to the policies of the SDS. The JNA remaining in Yugoslavia. Dismissals. Everything. Your Honours, if one looks, please, I would ask for that to come up, P138, we see that Mr. Brdjanin, although Mr. Radic, I think, was the president of this particular crisis staff, Radoslav Brdjanin, vice-president of the autonomous region told journalists, in addition, he stated: "The crisis committee is resolute in its implementation of all the demands that have so far been decided upon. All the changes in personnel will be decided by April 15th." Under what circumstances, as Mr. Dodik explained, under what circumstances would any government give in to demands by armed thugs unless it was because these armed thugs were working hand in glove with the authorities. Hand in glove to force onwards changes. Your Honour, again, there is a remarkable similarity between this, the SOS, at the almost identical period there's an SOS in Sanski Most. But later, when Teslic is not moving quickly enough with disarmament, with dismissals, what happens? This group, the Mice come in. They are as bad as, if not worse, than the SOS. And what happens? In the end, they're actually such a band of criminals that not only are they mistreating Muslims which I would suggest would not have bothered anybody in the slightest, but they are also mistreating Serbs. So the CSB is brought in to help clear these men out of Teslic. In Prnjavor, who goes in there? The Wolves of Vucak. Again, Your Honour, to clear the area. Your Honour, should there be any doubt of it, that is why we are somewhat surprised to see that the Defence still maintain or attempt to maintain this mantra that the SOS were a group of thugs, Mr. Radic himself in interview, when he was interviewed in Banja Luka, and affirmed this when he gave evidence before Your Honours - this is at transcript page 22247 - the interview was being put to him. "The way you put it, their appearance must have been orchestrated from somewhere. And you were asked who? And you said, yes, because the SOS couldn't appoint themselves." And he went on to say: "Someone had to prepare the territory, and the appearance of the SOS, there's a strange coincidence between that and the decision we received from Pale to form the crisis staff." And he gave an explanation of the decision. And Mr. Dodik, who was a reserve police officer who had been mobilised on duty at the airport, had expected an order to prevent them taking over the airport, he received no such order. And when he was pressed, he said had he been the authorities, he would have engaged the lawful police units and prevented the movement of those forces. Your Honour, the demand that the SOS made that there be -- "that Mr. Radic as president of the municipality activate a crisis staff that we would agree to and negotiate with." The persons appointed to the crisis staff were published in the newspaper, 137. And Your Honour, many familiar names appear on that crisis staff. Mr. Radic, Mr. Stevandic, I'll just check before I get somebody... Mr. Sajic, Mr. Kovacevic, Mr. Rosic, Mr. Vukic, and Radoslav Brdjanin, if one can put it that way, the mainstay of the later crisis staff. Your Honour, which is why we say this is a clear line from December of 1991 through until the 5th of May 1992. And Your Honour, on the 5th of April, the accused held another press conference. And Your Honour, I think we should look at that document. It's P139, because a complaint was made by the Defence that we were deliberately misquoting it. "On behalf of the crisis staff of the Banja Luka Municipality, Radoslav Brdjanin and Dr. Vukic, members of this staff," again, it's always Brdjanin and/or Vukic who were the spokespersons, "held a press conference today. For the most part, there was talk about the implementation of the already accepted requests of the Serbian Defence forces. Their requests have proved to be justified, especially now, said Brdjanin, because their objective is to protect the Serbian people from possible repetitions of the scenario from Bijeljina and Bosanski Brod." Your Honour, we copied the whole thing, lifted the whole thing and put it into the brief. The complaint was that we suggested that Brdjanin said everything. Well, Your Honour, this cannot be repeated in Banja Luka. It was said to date, we accept that it doesn't make it clear whether it's Brdjanin or Vukic, but it seems to be along the lines of the reporting from this conference, and we did not suggest, we simply lifted the quote in full. "And then for certain staff leveling changes, this will have to be done by the 15th of this month." Your Honour, and finally, to finish off this particular aspect, if we look at 2370, the day after the SOS come in, Karadzic in his role as president of the National Security Council is ordering the activation of crisis staffs in municipalities under specified conditions. And that's on the next page, if we can just go to that. And then finally, on the 27th of April 1992, Djeric issues his instructions, and we've already looked at those. Now, Your Honour, the ARK Crisis Staff, as it were, fons et origo, if one likes, of this case. The 5th of May decision is one by the executive council announcing the establishment. Now, it may be that there is another document because of the evidence Mr. Radic gave. This was at transcript page 21976, and it was his examination-in-chief. Question: "Just as a general proposition, from your perspective, observing the work of that crisis staff, what role did that ARK Crisis Staff play in the events in the Krajina between the 5th of May and the 17th of July 1992, if any?" "Well, before the war broke out, there was an association of municipalities. Then the AR Krajina was established. The goal was to exchange information on possible problems and help each other. That was the original goal. The crisis staff of the AR Krajina is not something that just turned up. It was not something that was created in Banja Luka by an individual. There is a document which reached us signed by the prime minister. And according to this document, the crisis staff was to be set up with certain obligations. However, this crisis staff did not carry out the tasks that had been set by that document. Let me even be so bold to claim that this was just a transfer of authority." Well, there were two things. Either there's another document specifically relating to the ARK Crisis Staff, or what Mr. Radic has in mind is the Djeric instructions, and he, like everyone else, look that to refer not only to the municipal but to the region. He was later asked, and this is at page 21983, again, still examination-in-chief: "What kind of mechanism did the ARK Crisis Staff have to enforce any of its decisions or conclusions? How could they enforce the decisions or conclusions that were issued by them?" Radic's reply: "I really don't know. As I said, they had received some sort of de jure authority. But as to whether they had any authority to force someone to implement something like that, I'm not aware of this." Now, Your Honour, the Defence make great play of the fact that it was Mr. Erceg who apparently formally announced, made the decision that this crisis staff was to set up, and the general consensus of those who were in a position to know is that such a decision did not lie within the competence of an executive council. Mr. Dzonlic was one of the witnesses who said that, of the assembly. And that, of course, begs the real question of the legality of any of this, as I've already dealt with. There are a number of unanswered questions in this case, and ones which to which we are never likely to get an answer. Why was the setting up the regional crisis staff done in this way? Was it a device? Mr. Erceg, who set up or signed the decision, is not someone that the Court's had the privilege of hearing from. There's some other unanswered questions, one I've already dealt with, where are the crisis staff minutes? Another really unanswered question, Your Honours may think, is why and how exactly did Mr. Brdjanin become the president of the ARK Crisis Staff? Most of the witnesses who should have been in a position to know professed ignorance or they speculated. Mr. Blagojevic said that his health, he thought, didn't allow him to take this position, referred to some meeting where Mr. Kupresanin had said that why should he get involved in all of this if the municipalities are going to take the decisions about dismissals? If it was his health, it didn't stop Mr. Kupresanin attending the assemblies of the Republika Srpska or indeed trotting around the various prison camps. What does that expression in the 29th of February ARK Assembly, and I think -- I hope that's on my list and we have got that in -- meeting. Just a moment. I think it's P -- yes, P35. Second page. That's the 29th of February. Third page, sorry. And Your Honour, we have been round the houses on that with some witnesses. Item 3: "Establish immediately strict control of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." Not one person who was there was able to explain to this Court what was meant by that conclusion; unable or didn't want to. And Your Honour, while we're on that topic there, we can see a request from Television Banja Luka for money. Your Honour, as I say, that's just one of a few questions that Your Honours are never going to have a direct answer to from the evidence and all that one can do from there is draw inferences from, really, the surrounding circumstances. And the inference we would invite you to draw from that conclusion is that it means exactly what it says, that there was going to be an imposition of force in order to obtain strict control of the territory. Now, Your Honour, if we can go back to the crisis staff list, P227, this is the official one published in the Gazette - thank you - now, Your Honour, as we say, the strict legal position was, those who were listed as members of the crisis staff held the highest position of authority. The Defence attempted to say that because all of the members were based in Banja Luka, this was throughout the trial, it's not something they repeat in their final brief, it was a local institution. So it had no authority outside Banja Luka. Well, Your Honour, I didn't have to do the exercise that I did with so many witnesses all over again. Mr. Brdjanin, member of the assembly of the Republika Srpska or whatever it was called in those days and head of the crisis staff, commissioned for whatever it was called, relocating -- no, dismissing people. I can't remember the name of it now, but anyhow. Lieutenant Colonel Milorad Sajic, the head of the TO; Mr. Kupresanin, assembly member, president of the ARK; Mr. Erceg, president of the executive committee of the ARK Assembly; Mr. Radic, let me say nothing else; Dr. Vukic, SDS president; Dr. Milovan Milanovic, he was a member of the -- he was, I think, already by then the deputy vice-president of the Republika Srpska; General Talic; Major Jokic, the air force until General Ninkovic came on the scene; Mr. Zupljanin, the CSB; Dr. Mirjanic, the only, if I can put it, odd one out, and I'll come back to that in a minute; Mr. Puvacic, the public prosecutor; Mr. Rosic, the judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dubocanin, we venture to suggest on the evidence nothing but a thug, a member of the intervention squad; Mr. Stevandic, the SOKOL leader, again the leader, according to the Serbs' own investigations, of the SOS; Mr. Bulic, the police; and Nedeljko Kesic, head of the DSB, I think it was, but whatever it was, the intelligence side of the CSB. Your Honour, not one single person on that list with one exception, and that's number 11 - I'm sorry, in fact, he was the replacement, we had this before, he was the replacement for the one person that I will come on to - refused to go to the inaugural meeting or any of the later meetings even if they didn't attend on a regular basis. Not one person with one possible exception, and that was Dr. Kuzmanovic, issued a public denial that they were on this crisis staff or that they had anything to do with this crisis staff. The only person who presumably had some objection was Dr. Kuzmanovic who was replaced within a matter of two days by Dr. Mirjanic. And Mr. Radic, you will recall, that that was one of his complaints, that Mr. Blagojevic hadn't noted down his interventions properly in respect of the replacement. And Your Honour, what body could possible have more authority in the eyes of the public in the Bosnian Krajina whether Serb, Muslim, or Croat, than one composed of the highest representatives from every walk of life? Mr. Blagojevic, when we went through that list with him, Talic and Zupljanin, and two leading politicians said this, when it was put to him, again there's going to be an objection to that, it was taken out of context. "This crisis staff, therefore, had real authority, didn't it, Mr. Blagojevic?" "Well, by virtue of the office these people held, that would be the conclusion." And that, Your Honour, this is at transcript page 21881. And Your Honour, that, in fact, is also what Mr. Radic said when he was dealing with Mr. Brdjanin. Yes, he had authority. But it didn't come from the membership of the crisis staff. It came from his other positions. Your Honour, we don't dissent from that either. General Talic's authority didn't come from his membership of the crisis staff; it came because he was head of the hugest corps - the hugest, that's bad English - the largest corps in the JNA and in the VRS. But together, combined, all these men with their personal authorities from their other positions made this an authoritative institution. And to the people in Banja Luka, it was apparently had authority. Mr. Dzonlic said, and this is transcript page 2409, "I was not surprised when I saw that the police had to observe the decisions of the crisis staff because it is my opinion and also on the basis of the documents which I had at the time and which I was able to see," and I think he was then referring to the ones he had been shown here, "at the top of the pyramid of power was the staff of the autonomous region, and all bodies had to execute the decisions of the crisis staff, and to report back on tasks carried out and conclusions implemented further to instructions from the crisis staff. And I know that they placed themselves above the official organs of authority." Question: "And by the official organs of authority, what do you mean?" "I am referring to the various secretariats within the municipality such as the secretariat for national defence, for the economy, the police, the assembly of the municipality, the executive council of the municipality. I'm thinking of those bodies of authority." "Mr. Smalagic," and this is at transcript page 1970, "why didn't you complain to Mr. Brdjanin as president of the crisis staff, the ARK crisis staff?" "Well, we didn't have the courage in general terms. I'm not referring to security. And after all the statements he had made about us, to go and talk to him seemed to be quite futile." Your Honour, just pausing there for a moment -- oh, sorry. Pausing there for a moment, Your Honour -- I'm sorry, one of the issues that comes across -- the Defence have raised is that people went to talk to Mr. Radic rather than to Mr. Brdjanin. And Your Honour, we suggest this witness encapsulated what a number of other witnesses said; namely, he was making these statements about us. Why would we go and talk to him? Mr. Radic at least seemed more reasonable. Your Honour, the answer continued in this way after "talked to him seemed to be quite futile." "And also, we didn't want to skip levels, the municipal level, and go to him directly, because he could have helped us quite a lot. But all this came to nothing, because this municipal level was under the regional level after all, the regional crisis staff." Your Honour, BW-1, again, it was in closed session so I'm not going to refer to it, and I remembered that, which is at page T23402 [Realtime transcript read in error "T23042"], if I can just ask you to look at one of the questions and answers on that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Transcript page number 23402.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I asked you to repeat because I had heard you 234 in sequence, and the transcript says 23042. So that stands to be corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. Regrettably, this is what happens sometimes. One transposes numbers. That's what happened both in our brief and in the Defence brief. Mr. Radic, finally - I'm afraid that's all I can do today, but I want to move on to a different topic anyhow - again, he was confirming his interview in Banja Luka. You were shown the document that -- yes. You were shown the document that established the crisis staff, and you said it was confirmed at the assembly. It was confirmed at the assembly and the executive committee of the ARK. It was signed by Mr. Erceg. And then this is just the whole interview being put to him, which is in fact an exhibit, Your Honours, as well. "It was then put to you: 'Once the crisis staff came into existence on the 5th of May 1992, it was the highest authority as far as a governing body in the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct?' And you said" - referring to what it said in interview - "'Yes, because the Assembly of the Autonomous Region was then disbanded so that the only thing that remained were the assemblies of the towns.'" And then going on with that part, Your Honour, all of this is at page 22267 - perhaps that's the simplest way of dealing with it - and he then was asked: "Was the highest body of government authority at the time, once the assembly was established, it was the crisis staff of the autonomous region was the highest body of government authority at the time once the assembly was disbanded. Is that correct?" Answer: Yes. Question: "And the ARK crisis staff had direct control over the municipalities within the ARK; is that correct?" And his reply was: "Depending. It depended on the individual. It depended on the people in the municipalities. It varied because there are documents from which you can tell when exactly -- because the municipal assembly still existed." Now, Your Honour, it's that particular aspect that is seized upon by the Defence, and that's what I want to deal with first thing tomorrow, to suggest that the municipal crisis staff, and suggests in the face of evidence showing to the contrary, went their own way because it depended on the individual. And Your Honour, you will -- may think that the evidence, all told, from the witnesses who were on or associated with the crisis staff gave inherently contradictory evidence themselves about the authority of the regional crisis staff. Your Honour, that brings me nicely to the next part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner. Before we adjourn, is there anything you would like to... Nothing. Okay. All right. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning, same time, 9.00, I think here in Courtroom III. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of April, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
